newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper futures end down in dull trade.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper futures end down in dull trade.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended down on Monday in dull trade after a weak performance by copper on the London Metal Exchange (LME) on Friday, traders said.

A narrowing of nearby spreads and a further inventory increase knocked LME copper down to $2,309.50, from $2,311 per tonne. The red metal was seen holdin gabove $2,300 a tonne in early Monday LME trade.

Shanghai's most actively traded November 1997 contract ended at 21,050 yuan ($2,539) per tonne, down 170 yuan from 21,220 yuan. It opened at 21,210 and hit an intraday high of 21,300 and a low of 21,010 yuan per tonne.
August fell 100 yuan to 20,700, September 10 to 20,910, October 60 to 21,050, December 170 to 21,050 and the January 1997 contract 100 to 21,100 yuan per tonne.
Combined volume fell to 57,550 tonnes from 81,820 tonnes.
Copper opened mostly down and fell further on profit-taking, traders said.
"Major institutions did not trade actively today," one trader said. "Profit-taking from small institutions and retail investors pushed prices down."
"Technical charts show further falls are expected in the short term," another traders said.
Physical copper prices in Shanghai fell to 20,700 yuan from 20,800/20,900 at the opening session, dragged down by falls on the futures market.
Traders said they expected the November contract to find strong support at the 20,800-yuan level in the short term.
Aluminium ended up. August rose 330 yuan to 14,280, September 410 to 14,560, October 370 to 14,620, November 340 to 14,640 and December 410 to 14,410 yuan.
The rises followed a sharp spike on the LME that took aluminium to around 21-month highs on Friday and which were followed by expectations on ongoing strength on Monday.
In early Monday trade, after a stocks fall of 450 tonnes -- following falls of around 10,000 tonnes last week -- LME aluminium was seen holding firm at $1,740 a tonne.
In Shanghai, combined volume fell to 4,130 tonnes from 4,510 on Friday.
